findings.issue: The author WITHHELD portable cases because frozen LFortran failed them: array-section, vector-subscript-section, component-section and negative-step implied-DO DATA objects. gfortran passes all four and 8.6.7 p5/p8 back the expected order. Withholding hides defects and leaves portably testable facets pending under a false reason.
findings.resolution: Four fixtures shipped with order-discriminating values; recorded as LFortran expected failures.

findings.issue: Twelve compile-fail mutants (six mutants on two compilers) broke the 8.6.7 p8 count equality, i.e. became NON-CONFORMING, and so proved nothing about repeat semantics.
findings.resolution: Replaced by balanced substitutions that keep the lists equal in length but change the per-object values, so each mutant compiles and fails at run time.

findings.issue: Only four of nine fixtures had a remove-DATA probe.
findings.resolution: Every fixture now has a conforming replacement probe; the pointer probe retargets to another initialized target instead of leaving the association undefined.

adjudications: A vector-subscripted section is a permitted DATA object: C879 requires section subscripts to be constant expressions, [4,1,3] is a constant rank-one integer array constructor per 10.1.12, and it is duplicate-free, so the section is definable.
Z'35' in DATA for a default integer is 53 per 7.7 and 8.6.7 p11.
